title: The Original Creole Band and who went north first
summary: Garland and the interviewer work out that Freddie Keppard's Original Creole Band was the first out of New Orleans, its personnel, and where Dink Johnson fit.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And in the beginning, they're getting that after we got on there, Freddie Kemper and myself, and, and, uh, Marion Perrin's, we got on in, up there. And that's where the jazz, the Dixie, the jazz band. In other words, uh, they call it, uh, the jazz band.
The Creole band went over big, and the people was falling for that, you know, but the kids were coming out. I, I, I...

Was that the first band that went out of New Orleans? Freddie Kemper. Freddie Kemper's Creole band. Yeah. What they call the original Creole band. The original Creole band. And was the first one that left... That's the band. Freddie Kemper. The first one that went to Chicago, huh? Did they go to Chicago or New York?
They, they come right to Chicago first. Yeah. No, Chicago. No, they come to Chicago. You see?
That was about 1912 or 1911 or something like that? Let me see what that was.

That must have been around the first part. Around in, around in that time. Yeah, it was. Because, uh, Freddie and them left. Because when they left, they had Cantrell, not Cantrell, they had, uh, Freddie Kemper, and they had, uh, Eddie Vincent on trombone. And they had, uh...
And wasn't Dink Johnson in that band?

No. No. No. No. Dink Johnson brought to the band out after they was out there, you know, where they used to bass. Dink Johnson's brother, their brother played guitar by ours one played guitar. Uh-huh. They had him.
